summary: Round 2, MEASURED not read. 23 mutations of Lease.java run individually, each reverted, tree verified clean and the staged hash unchanged after every one. MAJOR 2 (stringField off-by-one) and MAJOR 3 (unchecked escaping decode) are VERIFIED FIXED -- each mutation now dies, killed by exactly the test written for it. MAJOR 4(a) is VERIFIED FIXED -- dropping either rejectUnrepresentable call dies, and all three character classes (quote, backslash, control) are individually constrained. The canonical re-encode comparison could not be fooled: duplicates, unknown fields, reordering, interior whitespace, leading zeros, non-ASCII digits and '+1' are all refused. Epoch and expiry semantics are fully constrained (>= to >, renew bumping the epoch, takeover +2, takeover argument swap, encode field-order swap, both boundary off-by-ones, isBlank to isEmpty -- each killed by one named test). Suite re-run: 449 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; 17 red records present. Tier T0, correct; no sleep, port, temp dir or mock. TWO results go the other way. MAJOR 4(b), which round 2 was asked to probe, FINDS ONE: the constructor still accepts a value whose round trip is not identity, silently, with the suite green -- F1. And MAJOR 1 is NOT fixed by the tests added for it: two of the three shape-guard mutations still survive, because the canonical check subsumes them and the tests assert only the exception type -- F2. F2 is minor because behaviour is correct under every single mutation; F1 is major because the production code is wrong right now.

findings.title: The constructor still accepts a value whose round trip is not identity: an unpaired surrogate is silently replaced by '?' and no test would notice
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED against the UNMUTATED staged code, no mutation needed -- the production code is already wrong and all 17 tests are green:
  Lease l = new Lease(1, "pod\uD800x", "e", 5L);   // ACCEPTED
  l.encode() -> {"epoch":1,"holderPodId":"pod?x","holderEndpoint":"e","expiresAtMillis":5}
  Lease.decode(l.encode()).holderPodId() -> "pod?x"   // codepoints [70,6f,64,3f,78]
  Lease.decode(l.encode()).equals(l) -> FALSE, and NOTHING THROWS.
String.getBytes(UTF_8) maps an unpaired surrogate to 0x3F, so the holder identity is silently rewritten. decode cannot catch it: the canonical comparison compares parsed.encode() against the ALREADY-MANGLED bytes, so it matches. This is the same defect class as round 1's quote case -- silent corruption of the field that answers 'who may write the commit chain' -- and it violates the invariant the constructor's own comment states at Lease.java:66 ('THE ENCODER CANNOT ESCAPE, so refuse what it cannot represent'). Reachability is low (a K8s POD_NAME is ASCII; malformed UTF-8 from the environment decodes to U+FFFD, which round-trips fine -- measured), but round 1's quote case was equally unreachable from a real pod name and was accepted as major then; the calibration should be the same. It is filed major rather than minor for one further reason, which is the author's own argument for fixing the quote case now: adding this refusal once M4.3b and M5 have written leases is a format change under non-negotiable 8, so it is now or never.
TEST-SIDE STATEMENT: no test asserts round-trip identity over the accepted domain of the constructor. aLeaseRoundTripsThroughItsEncoding (:25) and anEmptyHolderEndpointIsAccepted... (:145) each pin ONE ASCII value; aHolderFieldContainingJsonHostileCharactersIsRefused (:172) enumerates four hostile inputs and stops. The property that would have caught this is 'every value the constructor accepts satisfies decode(encode(l)).equals(l)'.
REMEDY (small -- this does not imply the commit is too big): one clause in rejectUnrepresentable rejecting an unpaired surrogate, plus "pod\uD800x" as a fifth element of the existing hostile array at :172. Note the precise property is UNPAIRED: a valid pair round-trips (measured, 'pod\uD83D\uDE00x' identity=true), so a blanket Character.isSurrogate would also refuse a legal non-BMP value -- that choice is the production reviewer's, but the tests must pin whichever is chosen. Also measured as ACCEPTED and round-tripping correctly, so not part of this finding: DEL 0x7f, U+2028, U+2029, NBSP, U+0085, U+FEFF, U+1680, U+2003, leading/trailing spaces.

findings.title: The two tests added for round-1 MAJOR 1 kill nothing: the three named guard mutations still leave the suite green
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED, three mutations of Lease.java run individually, :format:test --tests binjava.format.LeaseTest reporting total=17 failed=0 each time:
  (1) delete '|| s.charAt(s.length() - 1) != '}'' at :140  -> 17/17 GREEN. aLeaseTruncatedByASingleByteIsRefused still passes.
  (2) delete 's.charAt(0) != '{' ||' at :140                -> 17/17 GREEN. the noBrace half of the same test still passes.
  (3) delete stringField's 'if (at < 0) throw' at :174-176  -> 17/17 GREEN. aLeaseMissingAStringFieldIsRefused still passes.
So the exact mutations round 1 named survive the fix written for them. The reason is that the OTHER round-1 fix -- the canonical re-encode comparison at :166 -- subsumes all three: encode() always emits a leading '{', a trailing '}' and every field, so any input failing a shape guard also fails the canonical comparison. These are therefore EQUIVALENT MUTANTS with respect to behaviour (the refusal still happens; only the message differs), which is why this is minor and not major: no single mutation makes decode accept a truncated or field-missing lease, and I could not construct one (a fabricated holderPodId read from a wrong offset cannot re-encode to an input that lacks the field). The fabricated-holder scenario round 1 warned about is genuinely closed -- by the canonical check, not by these tests.
Only 's.length() < 2' is actually constrained: deleting it is killed by aMalformedOrTruncatedLeaseIsRefused (:126) via the empty byte[] case, because charAt(0) then throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException rather than IOException -- and that is a PRE-EXISTING test, not one of the two new ones.
The mechanism behind all three survivals is that every decode-failure assertion in this file is isInstanceOf(IOException.class) with no message constraint, so a guard whose job another guard also does is invisible. If the intent is to constrain the guards, assert which one fired -- hasMessageContaining("not a lease object") at :194-205 and hasMessageContaining("is missing holderPodId") at :207-219 kill all three mutations (that is the reading of 'behaviour' the row itself takes when it argues the object must be legible to an operator diagnosing a stuck cluster). The alternative reading -- the guards are now dead code and should go -- is the production reviewer's call, not mine.

findings.title: The MAJOR-3 class is only half tested: an unterminated string field is the one decode input that still routes to an unchecked exception, and nothing decodes one
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED. Mutation: delete 'if (end < 0) { throw new IOException("lease has an unterminated " + name...); }' at :180-182 -> total=17 failed=0, SUITE GREEN. But this is NOT an equivalent mutant, unlike F2's three: with the guard gone, s.substring(from, -1) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, which extends IndexOutOfBoundsException, NOT IllegalArgumentException -- so it is not caught by the wrap at :157 and escapes a method declared 'throws IOException', straight past M4.3b's catch (IOException) on the recovery path. That is exactly the defect round-1 MAJOR 3 named, in the sibling code path. Verified reachable: Lease.decode("{\"epoch\":1,\"holderPodId\":\"" .getBytes(UTF_8)) takes it, and a lease object truncated mid-string is the realistic shape of a partially-written or corrupt control object -- the scenario decode exists for. aStructurallyValidLeaseWithAnIllegalValueFails... (:221) covers only the constructor path (a negative epoch), and no test in the file decodes an input with an unterminated quoted value. Minor rather than major because the guard IS present and the current behaviour is correct; the finding is that a regression on it is invisible. One line in aLeaseMissingAStringFieldIsRefused closes it.
For completeness, answering round 2's question 'is the catch complete': I probed 19 crafted inputs against the unmutated code and every one produced IOException -- epoch overflow (99999999999999999999), '-' alone, '+1', arabic-indic digit U+0661, '{}', '{ }', a nested object where holderPodId's value belongs, a marker at the very end ('...,\"epoch\":}'), a dangling trailing quote, and a value truncated after a marker. Dropping longField's 'if (end == from)' guard at :197 also survives (17/17 green) but IS an equivalent mutant -- parseLong("") throws NumberFormatException, which the wrap at :162 already converts. So the unterminated-string path is the only genuine gap in the class.

findings.title: strip() is wholly unconstrained, and the leniency it buys -- a hand-edited lease with a trailing newline -- is untested and contradicts the comment beside it
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. Mutation: 'new String(bytes, UTF_8).strip()' -> 'new String(bytes, UTF_8)' at :139 -> total=17 failed=0, SUITE GREEN. Every fixture in the file is already whitespace-free, so nothing sees the difference. The behaviour it removes is real and someone will depend on it: measured against the unmutated code, decode ACCEPTS '   ' + canonical + '   ', '\n' + canonical + '\n' and a U+2028-wrapped canonical, all returning the correct Lease. A lease hand-edited with an editor has a trailing newline, and hand-editability is the stated justification for the whole hand-rolled JSON codec -- so this is the one leniency the design actually wants, and it is pinned by nothing. It also makes the comment at :159-165 ('refuses ... any REORDERING or stray whitespace') half wrong: interior whitespace is refused (measured, '{"epoch": 1,...}' -> IOException) but surrounding whitespace is accepted. duplicateUnknownOrReorderedFieldsAreRefused (:233) tests the other three properties in that comment and not this one. Either behaviour is defensible; neither is asserted.

findings.title: decode(null) throws NullPointerException, not IOException -- the round-1 MAJOR 3 contract has a second hole outside the try block
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED against the unmutated code: Lease.decode(null) -> java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot read the array length because "bytes" is null. The wrap added for MAJOR 3 starts at :143; 'new String(bytes, UTF_8)' at :139 runs before it, so a null argument escapes the declared 'throws IOException' exactly as the IllegalArgumentException used to. Whether that matters is a judgement call the production reviewer owns -- a null byte[] is arguably a programming error rather than a corrupt object, and no BinStore path is known to produce one, which is why this is minor and separate from F3. Recorded because round 2 asked specifically whether any other unchecked exception can still escape decode: this and F3's mutation path are the only two I found.

findings.title: The row's account of the round-1 test fixes is inaccurate for two of the four
findings.failure_scenario: Round 2 asked whether the row is honest. Two of its four claims are verified true by measurement -- 'the empty-endpoint test asserted an accessor echo ... a one-character off-by-one in the closing-quote search' (the off-by-one now dies, killed by anEmptyHolderEndpointIsAccepted...) and 'decode threw unchecked IllegalArgumentException' (removing the catch now dies). Two are not: 'the shape guards were unconstrained ... deleting the trailing-brace check left the suite green -- now truncated by ONE' asserts a fix that F2 measures as still green under the same mutation, and the same holds for the missing-string-field guard. The closing 'All fixed, each red-recorded against the exact defect' therefore overstates: for those two the exact defect is an equivalent mutant and cannot produce a red, so whatever red the records at 1788389580 and 1788389582 were earned against, it was not that mutation. The honest form is that the canonical comparison closed the hole and the two new tests pin the behaviour without discriminating the guards. This is the same class of overstatement the row already corrects once ('All 11 mutation verified' was called stronger than what was measured in round 1); the fix is a sentence, and per rule 11 it need not be fixed at all if the row is left alone -- but it should not be left claiming a mutation dies when it does not. Verified true, for the record: 'Suite 449, 0 failures' (re-run: 449 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped) and 17 red records present in .harness/tdd/red.json.

verified_this_round: MAJOR 2 FIXED: stringField's int end = s.indexOf('"', from) -> s.indexOf('"', from + 1) is KILLED by anEmptyHolderEndpointIsAcceptedBecauseM4HasNoPeerMeshToPublish. Measured 17/1 failed.

MAJOR 3 FIXED: replacing catch (IllegalArgumentException | NullPointerException) with a catch that cannot fire is KILLED by aStructurallyValidLeaseWithAnIllegalValueFailsAsIoNotIllegalArgument. Measured 17/1 failed.

MAJOR 4(a) FIXED: dropping both rejectUnrepresentable calls is KILLED by 2 tests; and each character class individually -- allow-quote KILLED (2 tests), allow-backslash KILLED, allow-control-char KILLED.

Canonical comparison CONSTRAINED: deleting it is KILLED by duplicateUnknownOrReorderedFieldsAreRefused. Could not be fooled -- duplicate field, unknown field, reordering, interior whitespace, leading-zero number, arabic-indic digit, '+1' and a quoted number all refused.

Epoch/expiry semantics CONSTRAINED, one named killer each: nowMillis >= -> > (expiryIsDecidedByTheSuppliedInstant...), renewedUntil epoch -> epoch+1 (renewingKeepsTheEpoch...), takenOverBy epoch+1 -> epoch+2 and podId/endpoint argument swap (takingOverBumpsTheEpochByExactlyOne...), encode field-order swap (theEncodingIsExactlyThisByteSequence...), epoch < 0 -> < -1 (aNegativeEpochIsRefused, plus the decode test), expiresAtMillis < 0 -> < -1 (aNegativeExpiryIsRefused), isBlank -> isEmpty (aBlankHolderPodIdIsRefused).

Redundancy check: theEncodingIsReadableJsonAnOperatorCanInterpret (:31) is NOT vacuous despite looking dominated by theEncodingIsExactlyThisByteSequence (:45) -- it uses different field values, so an encode() that hardcoded :45's values would pass :45 and fail :31. No vacuous test found among the 17.

Tier T0 (pure record, no store/socket/clock -- isExpiredAt takes the instant as a parameter, satisfying non-negotiable 7). No Thread.sleep, no fixed port, no system temp, no mock. testing.md rules 11-18 clean.
